title: Function templates with multiple template types
recap: Independent template parameters permit heterogeneous arguments. A single T parameter for both arguments normally requires compatible deduction of one T, not arbitrary mixed arguments.
Multiple type parameters do not disable arithmetic conversions. Convert at the intended stage when the domain calls for floating-point mathematical addition.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Practice function templates with multiple template types.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement sumAsDouble<T,U>(left,right), returning the mathematical sum as double. Convert each operand to double BEFORE adding so mixed signed/unsigned inputs do not wrap. Tested values are small integers or finite doubles and are exactly representable or checked within 1e-9.
hints: Cast both operands before the + operation.
Casting the final sum would be too late for a mixed-sign wraparound.
